items.title: Section: The Fifth Reasoning — Contemplating a Future That Has Not Even Arisen — and the Full Case for Mind's Grasp of the Non-Existent Concludes

items.zh: 隨逐雜染，無出離期。是名第四言論道理。又未來行尚無有生，何況有滅！然聖弟子於未來行，非不隨觀生滅而住。是名第五言論道理。由此證有緣無意識。復有所餘如是種類言論道理，證成定有緣無之識，如應當知。
items.en:
Fifth, the reasoning that establishes contemplative observation. Furthermore, future conditioned phenomena have not even arisen, how much less have they ceased — yet noble disciples, with respect to future phenomena, do not fail to dwell in the observation of their arising and ceasing. This is called the fifth line of reasoning.
Second, the conclusion. By this, a consciousness that takes the non-existent as its object is established.
Second, indicating there is more. There are furthermore other lines of reasoning of this same kind that confirm there is definitely a consciousness taking the non-existent as its object, which should be understood accordingly.

items.title: Section: "There Is Past Karma" — Not Because the Past Is Real, But Because the Store-Consciousness Never Breaks Its Thread

items.zh: 問：如世尊言：有過去業。若過去業體是無者，不應今時有一領納有損害受，或復不應有一領納無損害受。此何密意？答：過去生中淨不淨業已起、已滅，能感當來愛不愛果。此業種子攝受熏習，於行相續展轉不斷。世尊為顯如是相續，是故說言有過去業。
items.en:
Second, the meaning of there being past karma; first, raising the scriptural question. Question: as the Blessed One said, there is past karma. If the essential nature of past karma were non-existent, one should not now experience a harmful sensation, nor equally a harmless one, as its result. What is the hidden intention here?
Second, explaining the answer; first, revealing continuity. Answer: wholesome or unwholesome karma in a past life has already arisen and already ceased, yet is capable of bringing about a future desired or undesired result. This karmic seed is retained and infused, continuing without interruption within the ongoing continuity of conditioned existence. The Blessed One, to reveal precisely this continuity, spoke of there being past karma.

items.title: Section: Refuting Five Gods Who Supposedly Birth the World, and the Heretics Who Claim There Is No Cause at All

items.zh: 又佛世尊觀二義故，作如是說。一、為遮止不平等因論者意故，顯此道理。謂彼妄見從大自在、帝釋、梵王、自性、丈夫及所餘等，一切有情淨不淨轉。二、為遮止一切無因論者意故，顯此道理；謂彼妄見都無有因。一切有情淨不淨轉。
items.en:
Second, refuting outside theories; first, stating the two purposes. The Blessed One, considering two matters, spoke in this way.
Second, explaining the distinct purposes; first, refuting the theory of unequal cause; first, stating the purpose of this refutation. First, to refute the intention of those who hold the theory of unequal cause, this principle was revealed.
Second, refuting the theory of no cause; first, stating the purpose of this refutation. Second, to refute the intention of all who hold the theory that there is no cause whatsoever, this principle was revealed. Second, explaining their theory. Namely, their mistaken view that all beings' desirable and undesirable circumstances arise with no cause at all.

items.title: Section: Why Noble Disciples Dwell Without Longing for the Past or Hope for the Future — And Refuting Both Extremes at Once

items.zh: 問：如世尊言：有過去行，於彼行中，我具多聞聖弟子眾無顧戀住；有未來行，於彼行中，我具多聞聖弟子眾無希望住。此何密意？答：過去諸行，與果故有；未來諸行，攝因故有。所以者何？現在諸行三相所顯：一、是過去果性故；二、是未來因性故；三、自相相續不斷故。為顯此理，故佛世尊說如是言。又觀二義，故作是說。一、為遮斷於去來法實有執故，顯此道理。謂若去來諸行性相是實有者，不應由彼去來之性說言是有。二、為遮斷撥無執故，顯此道理。謂彼妄計：如去來世，現在亦爾，都無所有。
items.en:
Third, the meaning of there being past and future conditioned phenomena; first, raising the scriptural question. Question: as the Blessed One said, with respect to past conditioned phenomena, my learned noble disciples dwell without longing; with respect to future conditioned phenomena, my learned noble disciples dwell without hope. What is the hidden intention here?
Second, explaining the answer; first, revealing the correct principle; first, stating it. Answer: past conditioned phenomena are said to exist because they have yielded their result; future conditioned phenomena are said to exist because they contain their cause. Second, the question raised: why is this so? Third, the explanation: present conditioned phenomena are revealed through three aspects — first, they are the nature of a past result; second, they are the nature of a future cause; third, their own self-characteristic continues without interruption. Fourth, the conclusion: it was to reveal this very principle that the Blessed One spoke these words.
Second, refuting attachment to extremes; first, stating the two purposes. Furthermore, considering two matters, he spoke in this way. Second, revealing the distinct attachments; first, the attachment to past and future as substantially real; first, stating the purpose of refutation. First, to refute attachment to past and future phenomena as substantially real, this principle was revealed. Second, explaining the principle. If past and future conditioned phenomena's nature and characteristics were substantially real, one should not speak of their existence through the language of having-become-past or not-yet-arrived.
Second, the attachment that denies the present; first, stating the purpose of refutation. Second, to refute the attachment that denies everything, this principle was revealed. Second, explaining that attachment. Namely, their mistaken view that the present, like the past and future, is likewise entirely without existence.

items.title: Section: "There Are Three Time-Periods" Means Three States of a Seed — And the Old Servant Woman Who Once Was the Buddha's Mother

items.zh: 問：如世尊言：有過去界、有未來界、有現在界。此何密意？答：若已與果種子相續，名過去界；若未與果，當來種子相續，名未來界；若未與果，現在種子相續，名現在界。當知此中如是密意。若苾芻等於如是種子相續中而得善巧，名於彼彼一切法中證得無量種種自性諸界善巧。
items.en:
Fourth, the meaning of there being three time-elements; first, raising the scriptural question. Question: as the Blessed One said, there is a past element, a future element, and a present element. What is the hidden intention here?
Second, explaining the answer; first, revealing the hidden intention. Answer: a seed's continuity that has already yielded its result is called the past element; a seed's continuity not yet having yielded its result, yet to continue and arise in the future, is called the future element; a seed's continuity not yet having yielded its result, presently continuing now, is called the present element. One should understand the hidden intention accordingly.
Second, revealing the skillfulness this brings. If a monk becomes skilled in the continuity of seeds in this way, this is called attaining boundless skillfulness regarding the countless distinct natures and elements present within any and every phenomenon.

items.title: Section: The Third Topic Closes, the Fourth Opens — Arising, Ageing, Abiding, and Impermanence Have No Reality Apart from the Five Aggregates

items.zh: 復次，云何應知生、老、住、無常離色等蘊無別實有？謂已遮未來諸行實有性，當知亦遮生實有性。
items.en:
Fourth, mind-dissociated formations and the rest; first, the explanation; first, explaining the provisionally established phenomena; first, mind-dissociated formations; first, arising, ageing, abiding, and impermanence; first, distinguishing their establishment; first, the general question. Furthermore, how should one understand that arising, ageing, abiding, and impermanence have no separate substantial existence apart from the aggregates?
Second, explaining each individually; first, refuting attachment to their substantial reality; first, refuting through reasoning; first, taking up arising; first, discussing it with respect to conditioned phenomena; first, refuting the arising of future phenomena; first, stating it. Since future conditioned phenomena's substantial reality has already been refuted, one should know that the substantial reality of their arising is likewise refuted.

items.title: Section: Not Even the Present "Arising" Is Real — Only Each Phenomenon's Own Seed Ever Truly Generates Anything

items.zh: 生自無所有，云何能生所餘諸行。亦非現在生能生現在諸行。由此生相有差別名，所謂諸行若生、若起、若現在性，離此差別，生之異相定不可得。諸聰慧者不應說言：即由現在令彼諸行成現在性。所以者何？若作是說：生生諸行。當知義顯即現在性能成現在。又一切法各各別有自種子因，何須計有異生能生。又此生相，為即諸行生耶？為是諸行生因耶？若即諸行生者，計此生相能生諸行，由有生故，諸行得生，不應道理。若是諸行生因者，諸行生時於一一行便有二生。謂生能生，不應道理。如生，如是，老、住、無常，由此道理如應當知。故知生等於諸行中假施設有。
items.en:
Second, refuting present arising; first, stating the principle. Nor can a present arising generate present conditioned phenomena.
Second, extending this to the rest. As with arising, so too should ageing, abiding, and impermanence be understood by this same reasoning.
Second, concluding it is established. Therefore one should know that arising and the rest are provisionally designated as existing within conditioned phenomena.

items.title: Section: Four Names for One Passage — Arising, Ageing, Abiding, and Impermanence Defined

items.zh: 由有因故，諸行非本。自相始起，說名為生。後起諸行與前差別，說名為老。即彼諸行生位暫停，說名為住。生剎那後諸行相盡，說名為滅，亦名無常。
items.en:
Second, explaining how these names are established; first, arising. Because conditioned phenomena depend on a cause, they are neither without origin nor originally pre-existent. When their own characteristic first manifests, this is called arising.
Second, ageing. When a later phase of conditioned phenomena differs from an earlier phase, this is called ageing.
Third, abiding. This same conditioned phenomenon, at the stage of having arisen, momentarily continues — this is called abiding.
Fourth, impermanence. The moment after arising, a conditioned phenomenon's characteristic is exhausted — this is called cessation, and is also called impermanence.

blocks.text: If the past is gone, how does past karma bear fruit? The answer is the store-consciousness: seeds carry it forward.
Master Cháng Bǎi: future things have not yet appeared; in fact one observes an image arising in this present thought.
Master Cháng Bǎi: a deed is simply gone once past, but the seed planted in the store-consciousness continues without interruption; whatever has been done leaves a trace.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the theory of unequal cause says things arise from Maheśvara, Śakra, Brahmā, primal nature, or a cosmic person; the other theory says all arises without cause. The treatise rejects both.

subs.head: Past and future exist, in a sense

blocks.text: Past things exist "because they have yielded their result", future things "because they contain their cause". Master Cháng Bǎi: this present thought holds the past's result and the future's cause.

subs.head: Three times, three states of a seed

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: 界 here is seed; there are past, future, and present seeds.

Master Cháng Bǎi: "dissociated" means associated neither with mind nor with form; these are designations set up on changes of form and mind. Apart from the five aggregates, there is no separately real arising, ageing, abiding, or impermanence. Every conditioned thing arises from its own seed; why add another "arising" to produce it?

Arising: a phenomenon first appearing through a cause, not pre-existing. Master Cháng Bǎi: "having a cause" refutes arising without cause. Ageing: a later phase differing from an earlier one; Master Cháng Bǎi, ageing means change.
"Whatever has been done leaves a trace." It is a sober thought, and also a hopeful one: good deeds leave traces too.

quiz.q: Since the future has not arisen, how can noble disciples observe its arising and ceasing?
options: noble disciples have the divine eye and directly see what is to come
future phenomena are already real and simply have not reached the present, and noble disciples see their image in advance through the power of absorption
they accept the Buddha's words on faith without really observing
based on this present thought, an image-part arises from the seeing-part of consciousness, and one observes the image in one's own mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: future phenomena have not yet appeared, so their features cannot be clearly grasped; in fact one relies on this present thought, an image-part arising from the seeing-part of consciousness, and observes that image in one's own mind.

quiz.q: The English renders 於行相續 as "the ongoing continuity of conditioned existence." Following the Sub-commentary and Master Cháng Bǎi, what does 行 mean here?
options: the ripening consciousness, in ordinary beings the store-consciousness; karmic seeds continue on within it
the formations aggregate, that is, volition continuing unbroken
bodily, verbal, and mental action itself: in the state of an ordinary being the deed has never yet ceased at all
practice, that is, the noble path continuing unbroken
quiz.why: The Sub-commentary glosses 行 here as the ripening consciousness, and Master Cháng Bǎi adds that in ordinary beings this is the store-consciousness: karmic seeds there continue by their own kind until their result is received. The English "conditioned existence" is broader and leaves this out, though the Blessed One's words still do not make the past real.

quiz.q: The deed is past. How does Master Cháng Bǎi say it can still bring about a result?
options: karma never really passes; its substance remains real in the past period and, when the time comes, yields a result by itself
past karma is recorded by gods, who dispense the result when due
the deed is gone once past, but its seed constantly accompanies this present thought; whatever is done leaves a trace
karma is gone once past; the result is a chance meeting of present conditions
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a phenomenon is simply gone once past, but the seed infused in the store-consciousness constantly accompanies the present thought; whatever has been done leaves a trace, and the seed in the store-consciousness continues without interruption.

quiz.q: The Blessed One spoke to refute the theory of unequal cause. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say this theory maintains?
options: their mistaken view that there is no cause at all: all beings' desirable and undesirable circumstances simply occur of themselves, made by no one
good causes bring bad results and bad causes good ones
the present, like past and future, is entirely without existence
all phenomena arise not from conditions but from Maheśvara, Śakra, Brahmā, primal nature, a cosmic person, and the like
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the theory of unequal cause maintains that phenomena do not arise from causes and conditions but from Maheśvara, Śakra, Brahmā, primal nature, a cosmic person, and the like. The theory that all arises with no cause at all is the second matter refuted, and denial of the present belongs to a different passage.

quiz.q: In what sense are past and future conditioned phenomena said to exist?
options: past phenomena because they contain their cause; future phenomena because they have yielded their result
both are substantially real and differ only in function
past phenomena because they have yielded their result; future phenomena because they contain their cause
both exist somewhere apart from the present
quiz.why: The treatise answers that past phenomena exist because they have yielded their result, and future phenomena because they contain their cause. Master Cháng Bǎi: future conditioned phenomena are so called because the seed already exists now and will surely bring its result.

quiz.q: Present conditioned phenomena are revealed through three aspects. How does Master Cháng Bǎi sum this up?
options: this present thought is only the past's result and has no future
this present thought is only the future's cause, with no substance itself
this present thought contains the past's result and the future's cause, and also exists in the present
this present thought stands independent of past and future
quiz.why: The treatise lists three aspects: the nature of a past result, the nature of a future cause, and an own characteristic continuing without interruption. Master Cháng Bǎi sums up that this present thought contains the past's result and the future's cause, and also exists in the present.

quiz.q: What is the hidden intention of "there is a past realm, a future realm, and a present realm"? Note how the English renders 界 as "realm."
options: 界 means a world: past, future, and present each have a world, and phenomena travel among them
界 means seed: the continuity of seeds that have yielded, will yet yield, or have not yet yielded now
界 means the three realms of desire, form, and the formless
界 means the eighteen elements, six for each time-period
quiz.why: The treatise explains the three by the continuity of seeds. Master Cháng Bǎi: 界 is seed; there are past, future, and present seeds. The English "realm" hides this sense and invites the reader to picture a place, though it does keep "a seed's continuity" in the definition.

quiz.q: What does "dissociated" mean in mind-dissociated formations, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: associated neither with mind and factors nor with form; conditioned phenomena established on the changes of form and mind
not associated with mind and factors but associated with form; established on the changes of form alone, and so belonging to form
associated with nothing at all, and so unconditioned
not associated with wholesome minds, only with afflicted ones
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "dissociated" means not associated with mind and mental factors, and not associated with form either. These are conditioned phenomena established on the changes of form and mind, called mind-dissociated formations to distinguish them from the unconditioned.

quiz.q: Do arising, ageing, abiding, and impermanence have substance apart from the aggregates?
options: all four have substance apart from the aggregates and act upon phenomena
arising alone is real and the other three provisional
they have no separate reality apart from the aggregates, being provisionally designated within conditioned phenomena
all four are unconditioned and do not belong to conditioned phenomena
quiz.why: The treatise concludes that arising and the rest are provisionally designated within conditioned phenomena. Master Cháng Bǎi: apart from the five aggregates of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, no separately real arising, ageing, abiding, or impermanence can be found.

quiz.q: Why can a future "arising" not generate conditioned phenomena?
options: a future arising is too far away for its force to reach the present
a future arising must wait for its season
a future arising has already arisen and cannot do so again
a future arising has no reality of its own, so how could it generate anything else?
quiz.why: The treatise says that once the reality of future phenomena has been refuted, the reality of their arising is likewise refuted. Master Cháng Bǎi: a future arising has no reality itself, so how could it generate other conditioned phenomena?

quiz.q: A present "arising" cannot generate present phenomena either. What, then, really generates them?
options: the marks of arising and abiding working together
the flow of time pushing phenomena into being
the mark of ceasing of the former moment, which generates the next moment's phenomena
each phenomenon's own seed; why posit a mark of arising beyond the seeds?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: every conditioned phenomenon has its own seed as the cause from which it arises, so why insist that, beyond each phenomenon's own seed, there is yet another mark of arising that can generate it?

quiz.q: Regarding "because conditioned phenomena depend on a cause," what does Master Cháng Bǎi say the words "having a cause" refute?
options: a really existing mark of arising and of abiding
the views of eternalism and nihilism
a really existing past and future
arising without cause and arising spontaneously
quiz.why: The treatise defines arising as a phenomenon's own characteristic first manifesting through a cause, not being pre-existent. Master Cháng Bǎi: the phrase "having a cause" refutes arising without cause and spontaneous arising.

options: a brief continuation at the stage of arising
a later phase of conditioned phenomena differing from an earlier phase
a phenomenon's own characteristic being exhausted the moment after it arises
years increasing and the body declining
quiz.why: The treatise says a later phase differing from an earlier phase is called ageing. Master Cháng Bǎi: ageing means change. The other definitions belong to abiding and to impermanence, and bodily decline is only one of the kinds of ageing listed later.
